key_moments.description: Elizabeth gave birth to a son in her old age. Neighbors wanted to name him after his father, but she said he would be called John, and Zechariah wrote the same.
key_moments.title: Named John

key_moments.description: John preached in the wilderness of Judea, telling people to repent because heaven's kingdom was near. He wore camel's hair, ate locusts and honey from the wild, and baptized people in the Jordan.
key_moments.title: Preaches in the Wilderness

key_moments.description: Jesus came to be baptized, and John said he needed to be baptized by Jesus instead. When Jesus came up from the water, the Spirit came down like a dove and a voice from heaven spoke.
key_moments.title: Baptizing Jesus

key_moments.description: Seeing Jesus coming toward him, John called Him the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sin. The next day two of John's disciples heard him and followed Jesus.
key_moments.title: Calls Jesus the Lamb of God

key_moments.description: John told Herod it was not lawful for him to have his brother's wife, so Herod put him in prison. At Herod's birthday feast, the daughter of Herodias asked for John's head, and Herod had him beheaded.
key_moments.title: Beheaded by Herod

name: John
summary: The son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, sent by God to prepare the way for Jesus. He preached repentance, baptized people in the Jordan, and pointed others to Jesus as the Lamb of God.

key_moments.description: Jesus saw James and John in their boat mending their nets and called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants and followed Jesus.
key_moments.title: Leaving the Nets

key_moments.description: Jesus took Peter, John and James up a mountain to pray. As He prayed His face changed and His clothes shone, and Moses and Elijah talked with Him.
key_moments.title: Sees Jesus Changed on the Mountain

key_moments.description: Peter and John met a man lame from birth at the temple gate called Beautiful. Peter healed him in Jesus' name, and the man held on to them as the people ran together in wonder.
key_moments.title: Sees a Lame Man Healed at the Gate

key_moments.description: The rulers marveled at the boldness of Peter and John, though they were unschooled, ordinary men. Told to stop speaking about Jesus, they answered that they could not stop telling what they had seen and heard.
key_moments.title: Refuses to Stop Speaking of Jesus

name: John
summary: A fisherman, the son of Zebedee and brother of James, who became one of the twelve apostles. After Jesus rose, he and Peter healed a lame man and spoke boldly before the council.

key_moments.description: At Shechem the people asked Rehoboam to lighten the heavy yoke his father had put on them. He turned from the counsel of the old men, followed the young men, and promised them a heavier yoke.
key_moments.title: Answers the People Harshly

key_moments.description: Israel rejected the house of David and stoned Adoram, the officer over the tribute. Rehoboam fled to Jerusalem in his chariot, and only Judah followed the house of David.
key_moments.title: Loses the Northern Tribes

key_moments.description: Rehoboam gathered an army to win back the kingdom, but the LORD sent word by Shemaiah not to fight against their brothers. The people listened and went home.
key_moments.title: Told Not to Fight

key_moments.description: Shishak king of Egypt came against Jerusalem and took away the treasures, including the shields of gold Solomon had made. Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place.
key_moments.title: Replaces the Gold Shields with Bronze

name: Rehoboam
summary: The son of Solomon who became king after him. When he answered the people harshly, the tribes of Israel broke away, and he was left to reign over Judah from Jerusalem.

key_moments.description: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord on a high throne, with seraphim calling Him holy. A live coal touched his lips to take away his sin, and when the Lord asked who would go, Isaiah offered himself.
key_moments.title: Sees the Lord on His Throne

key_moments.description: When Syria and Israel threatened Judah, the LORD sent Isaiah to meet King Ahaz and tell him not to fear their plans. Isaiah then gave the sign of a virgin who would bear a son named Immanuel.
key_moments.title: Gives Ahaz the Sign of Immanuel

key_moments.description: The LORD told Isaiah to take off his sackcloth and shoes. He went about naked and barefoot for three years, as a sign of how Assyria would lead away the people of Egypt and Cush.
key_moments.title: Walks Barefoot for Three Years as a Sign

key_moments.description: When Assyria mocked the LORD, King Hezekiah's servants came to Isaiah. He told them the LORD said not to fear, for the king of Assyria would hear a rumor and go home.
key_moments.title: Tells Hezekiah Not to Fear Assyria

key_moments.description: Isaiah told the dying Hezekiah to set his house in order, but after the king prayed, the LORD sent Isaiah back to promise fifteen more years. As a sign, the shadow on the stairway of Ahaz went back ten steps.
key_moments.title: Promises Hezekiah Fifteen More Years

name: Isaiah
summary: A prophet, the son of Amoz, who saw visions about Judah and Jerusalem during the reigns of four kings, from Uzziah to Hezekiah. He brought the LORD's word to kings in times of war and sickness.

key_moments.description: Leah bore Jacob a sixth son and said God had given her a good dowry, and now her husband would dwell with her. She named him Zebulun.
key_moments.title: Born to Leah

key_moments.description: Zebulun went down to Egypt with his father Jacob and the whole family, along with his sons.
key_moments.title: Goes Down to Egypt

key_moments.description: Jacob said Zebulun would dwell by the seashore and become a harbor for ships, with his border reaching to Sidon.
key_moments.title: Blessed by Jacob

name: Zebulun
summary: Jacob's sixth son by Leah. Jacob said Zebulun would dwell by the seashore and become a harbor for ships.

key_moments.description: Leah gave her maid Zilpah to Jacob, and Zilpah bore him a son. Leah named the boy Gad, saying, “How fortunate!”
key_moments.title: Born to Zilpah

key_moments.description: Jacob said of Gad that a troop would overcome him, but in the end he would overcome.
key_moments.title: Blessed by Jacob

name: Gad
summary: A son of Jacob, born to Leah's maid Zilpah. His descendants became the tribe of Gad, who chose to settle on the east side of the Jordan.

key_moments.description: The LORD told Ezekiel to prophesy against Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. Gog would gather a great army with many nations and come against the land of Israel like a storm and a cloud.
key_moments.title: Gathers the Nations Against Israel

key_moments.description: When Gog came against Israel, the LORD's fury would rise. The land would shake greatly, and He would send pestilence, hail, fire and sulfur, so that many nations would know He is the LORD.
key_moments.title: Meets the LORD's Fury

key_moments.description: The LORD would give Gog a burial place in Israel, and there Gog and all his army would be buried. Israel would spend seven months burying them to cleanse the land.
key_moments.title: Buried in the Valley of Hamon-gog

name: Gog
summary: Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, was the one the LORD spoke against through Ezekiel. In later years he would come against Israel like a storm, and the LORD would defeat him and his army.

key_moments.description: Nahum said the LORD is slow to anger but takes vengeance on His enemies, and is a strong hold in the day of trouble. He told Judah the LORD would break its enemy's yoke, and to keep its feasts, for the wicked would pass through no more.
key_moments.title: Tells Judah Its Yoke Will Be Broken

key_moments.description: Nahum saw chariots raging in the streets and Nineveh's people fleeing as its treasure was taken. He cried woe to the city of blood full of lies and robbery, and said all who saw it would say, Nineveh is laid waste.
key_moments.title: Says Nineveh Will Be Laid Waste

name: Nahum
summary: A prophet from Elkosh whose whole book is a vision that Nineveh, the city of blood, would be laid waste. Scripture tells nothing more about him and names no one else alongside him.

key_moments.description: Bilhah, Rachel's maid, bore Jacob a second son. Rachel named him Naphtali, saying she had wrestled with her sister in her great struggles and won.
key_moments.title: Born to Bilhah

key_moments.description: Naphtali went down to Egypt with his father Jacob and the whole family, along with his sons.
key_moments.title: Goes Down to Egypt

key_moments.description: Jacob said Naphtali was a deer let loose who gives good words.
key_moments.title: Blessed by Jacob

name: Naphtali
summary: A son of Jacob, born to Bilhah, Rachel's maid. Jacob said Naphtali was a deer let loose who gives good words.

key_moments.description: Hezekiah did right like David his father. He took away the high places and smashed the bronze serpent Moses had made, because Israel had been burning incense to it.
key_moments.title: Breaking the Bronze Serpent

key_moments.description: Hezekiah took the king of Assyria's threatening letter into the LORD's house and spread it out before Him in prayer. That night the angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians, and Sennacherib went home to Nineveh.
key_moments.title: Spreads Assyria's Letter Before the LORD

key_moments.description: When Hezekiah was dying, he prayed and wept, and the LORD promised to heal him and add fifteen years to his life. As a sign, the shadow went back ten steps on the stairway of Ahaz.
key_moments.title: Given Fifteen More Years

key_moments.description: Hezekiah showed the messengers from Babylon everything in his storehouses. Isaiah then told him that all of it would one day be carried off to Babylon.
key_moments.title: Shows His Treasures to Babylon

key_moments.description: Hezekiah sent letters across Israel and Judah, calling people to Jerusalem to celebrate the passover. He prayed for those who were not clean, and the LORD heard him, and Jerusalem had its greatest joy since Solomon.
key_moments.title: Holds a Great Passover

name: Hezekiah
summary: A son of Ahaz who became king of Judah and trusted the LORD like no other king of Judah. When Assyria threatened Jerusalem, he prayed, and the LORD saved the city.

key_moments.description: When Abram left Haran for the land of Canaan, his nephew Lot went with him.
key_moments.title: Going with Abram

key_moments.description: Lot and Abram had too many flocks to live together, so Abram let Lot choose where to go. Lot chose the well-watered plain of Jordan and pitched his tent toward Sodom, where the men were very wicked.
key_moments.title: Choosing the Jordan Plain

key_moments.description: Kings at war carried off Lot and his goods from Sodom. Abram armed his trained servants, chased them, and brought Lot back.
key_moments.title: Rescued by Abram

key_moments.description: Two angels warned Lot that the LORD would destroy Sodom, and they led him, his wife and his two daughters out by the hand. As fire and sulfur fell, Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.
key_moments.title: Escape from Sodom

name: Lot
summary: Abraham's nephew, who traveled with him to Canaan and then chose to live near Sodom. When the LORD destroyed Sodom, angels led Lot and his family out, but his wife looked back.
